responsibilities: Design and implement data transformation workflows using dbt to create reusable, analysis/chatbot-ready data assets aligned with business requirements.
Collaborate with stakeholders to gather data and analytics needs, translating them into technical specifications and scalable data models.
Work closely with data engineers to build efficient, scalable, and reliable data models and pipelines for current and future use cases.
Implement data quality checks and monitoring processes to ensure data accuracy, consistency, and completeness.
Promote and support the adoption of software engineering best practices in analytics, including version control, code reviews, and automated testing to ensure code quality and readability.
Document data transformations and implement best practices.

evidence.velocity_vs_rigour: Implement data quality checks and monitoring processes to ensure data accuracy, consistency, and completeness.
evidence.velocity_vs_rigour_explanation: Quality and engineering discipline carry the responsibilities — data quality checks, plus "version control, code reviews, and automated testing" — with no speed or shipping language anywhere.
evidence.domain_risk: Collaborate with stakeholders to gather data and analytics needs, translating them into technical specifications and scalable data models.
evidence.domain_risk_explanation: The finance placement sits in the job title only; the responsibilities never name financial reporting, audit or regulatory work, so the stated stakes are ordinary business decisions.
evidence.data_team_maturity: Work closely with data engineers to build efficient, scalable, and reliable data models and pipelines for current and future use cases.
evidence.data_team_maturity_explanation: A separate data engineering function already exists and dbt is in the responsibilities, but the hire still has to "promote and support the adoption of software engineering best practices in analytics" — growing, not settled.
evidence.jd_authorship: Collaborate with stakeholders to gather data and analytics needs, translating them into technical specifications and scalable data models.
evidence.jd_authorship_explanation: Half the bullets are portable boilerplate like this one and "Document data transformations and implement best practices", half name real tooling and outputs.
evidence.stakeholder_orientation: Work closely with data engineers to build efficient, scalable, and reliable data models and pipelines for current and future use cases.
evidence.stakeholder_orientation_explanation: The only partner named in the responsibilities is the data engineering function, and the output is "reusable, analysis/chatbot-ready data assets" for downstream data consumers.
evidence.autonomy_level: translating them into technical specifications and scalable data models
evidence.autonomy_level_explanation: Work arrives as gathered needs and business requirements for the hire to specify and build; no bullet gives them direction-setting over the data agenda.
evidence.ai_role_explanation: The first responsibility is building dbt models that a chatbot consumes, so the hire's output feeds an AI system rather than the hire being expected to use AI tools.
evidence.testing_framing: Implement data quality checks and monitoring processes to ensure data accuracy, consistency, and completeness.
evidence.testing_framing_explanation: Quality checks and automated testing are responsibilities the hire implements and champions, not tools listed in a skills section.
evidence.loss_aversion_framing: to ensure data accuracy, consistency, and completeness
evidence.loss_aversion_framing_explanation: The fear is inaccurate or incomplete data reaching users, framed as one operational bullet among six rather than as the role's organising risk.
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix: Design and implement data transformation workflows using dbt to create reusable, analysis/chatbot-ready data assets aligned with business requirements.
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix_explanation: Every infrastructure verb is build-oriented — design, implement, build "for current and future use cases" — with no migration, cleanup or legacy language.
evidence.language_gate: Excellent written and spoken English communication skills;
evidence.work_arrangement: Work from anywhere: work from wherever keeps you in the zone.
evidence.loss_aversion: Reliability framing is operational rather than regulatory: "Implement data quality checks and monitoring processes to ensure data accuracy, consistency, and completeness."
ats_keywords: version control, code reviews, and automated testing
